mechanism_narrative: The ongoing rebound in WORKPLACES mobility from -20.6 to -11.7 implies more weekday commuting and lunch-time spillovers. That should lift RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks relative to the last four weeks if the workplace gains persist.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC remains at or below the last-4-week mean despite WORKPLACES staying above its t-1w level for the next two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT moves above its pre-shift plateau while WORKPLACES continues rising, access to central shopping and dining zones improves and retail visits increase within two weeks. The mechanism is directional only when both commuter and transit activity strengthen together.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises above 0 after being negative in the prior week
failure_condition: TRANSIT turns positive but RETAIL_REC does not rise over the next 14 days while WORKPLACES also continues increasing.

mechanism_narrative: Persistent elevation in RESIDENTIAL mobility alongside weak WORKPLACES indicates more time spent near home. That substitution reduces discretionary retail trips, so RETAIL_REC should fall over the next four weeks relative to the prior four-week average.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 28 days while RESIDENTIAL stays above 5 and WORKPLACES fails to recover materially.

mechanism_narrative: A further drop in PARKS below its current low range signals less discretionary out-of-home activity, which should spill over into weaker retail-and-recreation visits within one week. The effect is strongest when park mobility falls sharply from an already depressed level.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls below -22 after two consecutive weeks above -21
failure_condition: PARKS drops below -22 and RETAIL_REC does not decline within 7 days.

mechanism_narrative: If GROCERY_PHARM stays strongly positive while TRANSIT remains near zero or negative, consumers are likely consolidating essential trips and avoiding multi-purpose shopping outings. Under that constraint, RETAIL_REC should stay flat to lower over four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT stays at or below 0 while GROCERY_PHARM remains above 20
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days despite GROCERY_PHARM staying above 20 and TRANSIT not recovering above 0.

mechanism_narrative: A continued improvement in TRANSIT mobility indicates easier access to shopping corridors and entertainment districts. When transit demand keeps rising for two consecutive weeks, RETAIL_REC should follow with a lag of about two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT increases for two consecutive weeks from a negative base
failure_condition: TRANSIT rises for two straight weeks but RETAIL_REC is not higher after 14 days than its level at the trigger week.

mechanism_narrative: When PARKS and RETAIL_REC move in opposite directions, the pattern reflects a seasonal substitution from outdoor leisure back to indoor retail-and-recreation venues. If PARKS remains weak while GROCERY_PHARM stays elevated, retail should strengthen over the next month.
candidate_trigger: PARKS remains below -19 while GROCERY_PHARM stays above 20
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise over 28 days even though PARKS stays depressed and GROCERY_PHARM stays above 20.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous easing in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT signals broader reopening of movement networks that directly feeds discretionary retail traffic. Because WORKPLACES is still rising from a low base, the effect should appear within four weeks only if transit also continues to recover.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises above -1 while WORKPLACES improves for three consecutive weeks
failure_condition: WORKPLACES keeps improving and TRANSIT rises above -1, but RETAIL_REC does not exceed its last-4-week mean by the end of 28 days.
